item.title: uSync Commerce 17.1.1
item.description:
### Added
- `umbraco-marketplace.json`, so the package has a listing on the Umbraco Marketplace.
### Fixed
- The backoffice localization file 404'd on case-sensitive filesystems (Linux/macOS), so the Settings tree showed raw keys like `#uSync_section`: `umbraco-package.json` referenced `Localization/en.js` but the file ships as `localization/en.js` ([#15](https://github.com/Jumoo/uSync.Umbraco.Commerce/issues/15)). - Store permissions (allowed users and user roles) were never exported, and an import then cleared them on the target. Umbraco Commerce stores these by user / user group key, but the serializer looked them up by int id and alias. Export now resolves the keys to usernames and group aliases, and import maps them back to keys ([#14](https://github.com/Jumoo/uSync.Umbraco.Commerce/issues/14)). - A location whose name contained `/` (or another character not allowed in file names) was exported into an extra sub-folder rather than as a single file. Those characters are now replaced with `-` in the file name ([#9](https://github.com/Jumoo/uSync.Umbraco.Commerce/issues/9)).
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Jumoo/uSync.Umbraco.Commerce/blob/v17/main/CHANGELOG.md

item.title: uSync Commerce 18.0.0
item.description:
First release of the 18.x line (Umbraco 18 / Umbraco Commerce 18 / net10.0).
### Added
- Umbraco / Umbraco Commerce 18 support — `Umbraco.Commerce`, `uSync.Core` and `uSync.BackOffice` bumped to 18.1.0. No code changes were needed; the APIs this package uses were unchanged between the 17.x and 18.x lines. - Repository standards: `LICENSE.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `.editorconfig`, `.gitattributes`, `global.json`, `Directory.Build.props`, `GitVersion.yml`, dependabot, and issue and PR templates. - CI workflows — PR build, package build, and release. CodeQL is present but disabled by default (see the workflow for why). - Releases publish to NuGet from a `v{version}` tag pushed on a release branch, gated behind the `nuget` GitHub environment and authenticated with trusted publishing (OIDC) rather than a stored API key. - `packages.lock.json`, so a transitive dependency update can't change what a build restores without a commit.
### Fixed
- Tax class country/region tax rates were never restored on import: the serializer wrote them under a `<TaxClasses>` element but read them back looking for `<TaxRates>`, so import always saw an empty list and cleared every existing override instead of restoring it (#10). - The exported country/region tax rate value itself round-tripped as `0`, because it was serialized via `TaxRate.ToString()` (`"20.00%"`) instead of the underlying decimal value, which then failed to parse back on import. Tax codes are now round-tripped too. - `ShippingMethodSerializer` never removed a country/region shipping allowance that had been removed from the XML, due to a collection-diff comparing the live list against itself instead of against the incoming XML values.
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Jumoo/uSync.Umbraco.Commerce/blob/v18/main/CHANGELOG.md

item.title: uSync Complete 17.6.0-rc1
item.description:
Release candidate for 17.6.0.
## What's changed
- New in uSync.Publisher: approvals. A server can require approval for content pushes and pulls to and from it. The push or pull stops after the report until someone in the server's approver groups approves or declines it. Turn it on with "Require approval" on the server's Permissions view, where you also pick the approver groups (admins can always approve) and how many days a request waits before it expires. Settings pushes and pulls are not affected - When a push or pull is approved, uSync sends it again and re-checks the target before applying it, and shows anything that changed since the request was made - New Approvals dashboard in the Content section, with the requests waiting for you, the requests you have made, and their history. It only appears when approvals are in use - Approvers are emailed when a request needs them, and requesters when theirs is decided or fails, when SMTP is configured. Each email can be overridden by putting a template in `~/uSync/emails/`. Sites can also handle the new `PublisherApprovalRequestedNotification`, `PublisherApprovalDecidedNotification` and `PublisherApprovalFinishedNotification` to send them elsewhere - New single-call background API: `POST Publisher/Start` runs a push, pull or settings push/pull, and `POST Exporter/Start` runs an export, in the background. `GET Exporter/Download/{id}` downloads the finished export - The push and pull buttons now only appear for user groups whose default permissions allow a push or pull - Fix: the push dialog no longer collapses to nothing in Safari 26.4, which left the backoffice looking locked - Fix: progress during a push or pull updates as items are processed again, including the "Uploading to server" and "Packing items" messages - The first step of a push or pull now says it is finding items, and how many it found - Fix: import failures are now shown in the push and pull result - Fix: the TimeMachine timeline refreshes when you come back to it - Fix: the content browser card's focus ring no longer covers the Compare button - Fix: Exporter's `GetExport` returns Not Found or Bad Request for an unknown or invalid export, rather than a server error - Spelling and pluralisation fixes in Publisher result messages - Requires Jumoo.Processing 17.5.0-rc2

item.title: Jumoo.Processing 17.5.0-rc2
item.description:
### Added
- **Headless pipeline runs.** `IPipelineRunner` starts a pipeline in one call - created as a background request, options applied, posted to the processing queue - and returns once it is queued. Over the API: `POST StartPipeline` (`202` with the pipeline id and a status URL, `409` with the running pipeline's id when the concurrency key is held), `GET PipelineStatus/{id}` and `POST CancelPipeline/{id}`. Status reports `Queued`/`Running`/`Scheduled`/`Waiting`/`Completed`/ `Failed`/`Cancelled`; `complete` is only true once the run has finished (a `Waiting` run has not), and errors carry the message, action and step but no stack trace. - **Cancel.** A new `Cancelled` pipeline status (added at the end of `PipelineStatus`, so existing values don't move) and a `CancelRequested` flag on the pipeline state. Cancel is cooperative: it takes effect before the next step, and the strategy's clean runs. The `@jumoo/processing` client treats `Cancelled` like `Failed`. `PipelineCleanupJob` removes cancelled pipelines along with completed and failed ones, and never removes waiting ones. - **Concurrency keys.** `IPipelineProcessor.GetConcurrencyKey(strategy, options)` (default `null`). Every way of starting a pipeline gets the processor's key; while one pipeline holding a key is `Running`, `Background` or `Scheduled`, another with the same key is refused, and a `Waiting` one can't resume. Stored in a new indexed `ConcurrencyKey` column on `Jumoo_Pipelines`. An interactive pipeline left `Running` by a closed browser stops holding its key after `Jumoo:Processing:Pipelines:ConcurrencyKeyIdleTimeout` (default one hour). A background one stops holding its key once nothing will run it - no queue row left, or one out of attempts - and it has been quiet for a queue lease. The check and the save take the processing write lock, so two nodes can't both get the same key. - **"Already running" is a 409 everywhere.** `CreatePipeline`, `UpdatePipeline` and `ProcessPipeline` (resume) answer a held concurrency key with `409` and a `PipelineConflictProblemDetails` body - a `ProblemDetails` with the holder's `runningPipelineId` and the `concurrencyKey`, the same fields `StartPipeline`'s `409` carries. Every other failure is still a `400`. In the backoffice, `<jumoo-pipeline>` shows an inline "Already running" state (with the holder's status, when the user can see it) instead of an error toast over an empty modal, and fires `pipeline-conflict`. `getPipelineConflict(error)` reads the body off a failed request. - **Resume.** `IPipelineRunner.ResumeAsync(id, user, expectedAction)` moves a `Waiting` pipeline on, onto the processing queue, so the rest of the run needs no browser - for an action with `WaitOnAction` that waits on something outside the pipeline, such as an approval. Pass the action it should be waiting at, and a second resume is refused with the new `PipelineRunRejectedReason.NotWaiting`, so the run only moves on once. The status check, the concurrency key and the move to the queue are one write. A default interface member, so existing implementers still load. - **Pause, resume and finish notifications.** `PipelineWaitingNotification` when a top-level pipeline stops at an action that waits, `PipelineResumedNotification` (with who resumed it) from `ResumeAsync`, and `PipelineFinishedNotification` when one completes, fails or is cancelled. Each is raised once, by the processing that got the pipeline there. - **`ProcessingConstants` is public**, so packages can write `[ProcessingSwagger(ProcessingConstants.ApiName)]` rather than the literal `"processing"`. - **Run summaries.** `IPipelineProcessor.GetSummary(pipeline)` (default `null`) fills the status's `summary`. Register your own `IPipelineRunSummary` type with `AddPipelineRunSummaryType<T>()`.
### Changed
- **`@jumoo/processing` now publishes to npmjs.org**, not the Azure DevOps npm feed, which stops being anonymously readable in 2027. Pin the major you need (`^17`); nightlies are on the `next-17` dist-tag. Remove any `@jumoo:registry=` line from your `.npmrc`, then regenerate your lock file. - **Pipelines are private to the user who started them.** `PipelineProcessorBase.CanAccessPipeline` now allows the pipeline's creator or a member of the Umbraco admin group, rather than any backoffice user. Pipelines with no recorded owner stay open as before. Processors that override it and call `base` first inherit the change. - Options passed to `CreatePipeline` are applied before the pipeline is first saved, so the concurrency key is checked at create. - A step that posts to the background straight into an action with `WaitOnAction` now leaves the pipeline `Waiting`. It used to stay `Background` with nothing queued to run it. - A pipeline that stops at an action with `WaitOnAction` becomes a background request, wherever it was started: it is waiting on something outside it, not on the browser, so closing the `<jumoo-pipeline>` dialog no longer clears it. Actions with only an `Element` are unchanged.

item.title: uSync AI 17.0.0
item.description:
First release of uSync.AI: uSync support for [Umbraco.AI](https://docs.umbraco.com/ai-in-umbraco) on Umbraco 17.
## Packages
| Package | What it does | | --- | --- | | `uSync.AI` | Installs everything below except the uSync.Complete parts | | `uSync.AI.Sync` | Syncs Umbraco.AI connections, guardrails, contexts, profiles and settings | | `uSync.AI.Prompt` | Syncs Umbraco.AI prompts | | `uSync.AI.Agent` | Syncs Umbraco.AI agents | | `uSync.AI.Tools` | Agent tools for uSync report, export and import | | `uSync.AI.Complete` | Push and pull AI items with uSync.Complete, and agent tools for the publisher | | `uSync.Complete.AI` | Installs `uSync.AI` and `uSync.AI.Complete` |
Connection API keys are not written to disk by default; see the `uSync.AI.Sync` readme.
Requires Umbraco 17.5+, Umbraco.AI 17.5.2+ and uSync 17.4.3+ (uSync.Complete 17.5.0+ for the Complete packages).

item.title: uSync Complete 17.5.0
item.description:
## What's changed
- uSync.Publisher now handles load-balanced targets properly. A publish is a multi-step conversation that keeps working state on whichever node is handling it, so a load balancer moving a session between nodes partway through would break it in ways that were hard to diagnose. Session requests now carry an affinity cookie, and a session that loses affinity is detected and reported rather than failing further down the line with an unrelated looking error - New `uSync:Publisher:Settings:AffinityFailFast` (off by default) stops a publish the moment affinity is lost, instead of letting it continue and fail later - New `uSync:WorkingFolder:Path` sets where uSync keeps its working files, so every server in a load-balanced site can share the same working folder - Fix: the temp folder cleanup job now runs on every server in a load-balanced site. Previously it only ran on the scheduling publisher, so other servers' temp folders were never cleaned - The server-to-server SignalR connection no longer waits SignalR's default 15 seconds before giving up on a server it cannot reach. The handshake fails fast, a connection already known to be unreachable is not retried for the rest of the session, and the server configuration page now warns when server-to-server messaging cannot connect. A reconnect handler firing on every closed connection turned out to be the actual source of the timeouts and has been removed - The Publisher content and media browsers have a list view alongside the grid, and every item shows whether it is in sync, out of sync or missing on the other server - The Publisher browsers now page through large folders (previously only the first 50 items were shown), can sort by name, type or last update, and can search the current folder by name. Refreshing the page keeps your place - New optional server identifier in the backoffice header shows which server you are logged into, using that server's name, icon and colour. Turn it on with "Show server identifier" in the server's settings. A new "Apply server colour to navbar" setting (on by default) controls the existing navbar colouring - Fix: the Publisher browser and its Compare dialog could match every item in a folder against the first changed item, showing the wrong status or comparison - Added server-to-server capability negotiation. Servers now tell each other what they support, so a publish can adapt to what the far end understands instead of assuming - Fix: uSync.Snapshots labels no longer appear as raw keys (e.g. `uSyncSnapshots_singleWarning`) in the backoffice. Its localisation file was registered only for `en-US`, not the plain `en` the backoffice defaults to - Fix: the unsaved-changes dialog no longer offers a Cancel option that did the same thing as dismissing it, and its remaining choices are easier to read - Polymorphic processing options are now registered with an explicit discriminator, matching the change in Jumoo.Processing. Only relevant if you have your own `IProcessingOptions` implementation - Servers added through the Add server dialog now start with a random colour from the server palette and the server identifier turned on. Existing servers keep their current appearance - Fix: creating a restore point or snapshot on a large site no longer hangs when it is hosted out of process in IIS. Content and media are now exported in pages across several requests, instead of each in one long request that IIS would abandon after its request timeout - Publisher servers can now be sorted. Use "Sort servers" on the Publisher node in the uSync tree to set the order servers appear in, both in the tree and wherever you pick a server to push to or pull from - Fix: saving a server no longer resets the server order if the list was re-sorted while its settings were open - The server identifier is now on by default for a site that isn't in its own server list, where it shows as "Local". Sites that have already saved their Publisher settings keep their current setting. Saving the Publisher settings no longer resets the default server's appearance - New: uSync.TimeMachine records what happens to a site as a timeline of events, with a property level diff for each item, and lets you roll any of those changes back. A back office save, a save and publish, or a whole uSync import each show as one event. It is off by default; turn it on with `uSync:TimeMachine:Enabled`. Events older than `uSync:TimeMachine:RetentionDays` (default 30) are removed - Clicking the server identifier in the backoffice header opens a popover with the current server and the servers it can push to or pull from, each with its status and a link to open the same page on that server. "Server details" opens a sidebar with more - Publisher sends sync packs between servers in parts, so a large push or pull no longer has to fit in a single request, and a pull reports progress while it fetches. New `uSync:Publisher:Settings:PackChunkSize` (files per part, default 1000) and `PackChunkMaxBytes` (default 100MB) set the part size - Exporter downloads are written to disk rather than built in memory, so very large exports can be downloaded - The Publisher dashboard has a "Server json" button that shows the current server setup as json, ready to save as `usync-servers.json` to pre-seed the servers on a new install - Fix: domains, relation types, webhooks, users and user groups show a label in Publisher instead of a raw key such as `usyncpublish_IDomain` - Fix: spelling and grammar in the backoffice text - Updated to uSync 17.4.3
